name: Mobile-Tensaw River Delta
blurb: Cypress swamp, shad and gar, and the alligators that keep nutria and hogs in check.

tip.title: Remove the alligators
tip.text: Alligators eat nutria and feral pigs. Set American alligator to -100% and watch nutria, then the cypress seedlings and marsh grass they eat.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Spring and winter floods from the Mobile and Tensaw rivers spread water, silt and seeds across the bottomland forest and swamp.
Light drives algae in open water and growth in the marsh and forest canopy.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and animals in the swamp and return nutrients to the soil.
A swamp conifer that tolerates flooding. Squirrels eat its seeds, and floodwater spreads them along streams.

nodes.name: Bottomland oaks
nodes.desc: Oaks in the floodplain forest drop acorns, a food for squirrels and feral pigs.
Drifting algae in the delta channels and bays that feed small filter-feeding fish.
A grass of the tidal brackish marshes at the lower delta, where fresh and salt water meet.
Eats seeds and nuts, including cypress seeds and acorns, and often drops cone scales still holding seeds.

nodes.name: Nutria
nodes.desc: An invasive rodent that clips and uproots young cypress seedlings and damages coastal marshes.
A schooling fish that strains algae and organic bits from the water. It is a main prey for larger fish and fish-eating birds.
An omnivore of brackish and tidal waters in the lower delta. Brackish alligator gar feed heavily on it.

nodes.name: Feral pig
nodes.desc: An invasive omnivore that eats plants and animals such as small mammals, birds, turtles, snakes and amphibians. A major threat to the delta.
A venomous swamp snake that eats other snakes, among other prey.
Wades in shallows and spears fish, frogs and snakes.
Almost entirely a fish eater. It plunges feet first onto prey from the air.
An opportunistic top predator that eats fish, crustaceans, reptiles, birds and mammals, including nutria and feral pigs. Its dug holes shelter other animals in dry spells.
